#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

According to this [code](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/bbe8ca8b2ab14992389bc67e3bcfa209adcb13d4/pkg/apis/core/validation/validation.go#L4996), the QosClass of pod status is immutable.

This [function ](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/40b604e374144351eac463e7077fdb1903f5a033/pkg/apis/core/helper/qos/qos.go#L48)also shows that QosClass is computed from the resources instead of being provided by users.

However, we can use rest api or "kubectl edit pod --subresource='status'" to change it.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

```release-note
Tighten validation on the qosClass field of pod status. This field is immutable but it would be populated with the old status by kube-apiserver if it is unset in the new status when updating this field via the status subsource.
```

issue_context.title: QosClass of pod status shouldn't be changeable
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

According to this [code](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/bbe8ca8b2ab14992389bc67e3bcfa209adcb13d4/pkg/apis/core/validation/validation.go#L4996), the QosClass of pod status is immutable. 

This [function ](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/40b604e374144351eac463e7077fdb1903f5a033/pkg/apis/core/helper/qos/qos.go#L48
)also shows that QosClass is computed from the resources instead of being provided by users. 


However, we can use rest api or "kubectl edit pod <podName> --subresource='status'" to change it. 




### What did you expect to happen?

The request to change QoSClass of pod status should receive a validation error to indicate it's immutable. 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Use "kubectl edit pod <podName> --subresource='status'" to change the qosClass to a different value. It will succeed. 

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

In fact, this value cannot be changed. It directly obtains the qos of the old pod and compares it with the calculated value of the new pod. It does not matter what value is changed, and the change will not succeed.

`edit` succeed, but get pod still the old status qos

> In fact, this value cannot be changed. It directly obtains the qos of the old pod and compares it with the calculated value of the new pod. It does not matter what value is changed, and the change will not succeed.
> 
> `edit` succeed, but get pod still the old status qos

@chengjoey Not exactly. If you use "--subresource=status" in "kube edit po", it can change the qosClass. I verified that on 1.29.4.

/unassign

I did not look into this.

/assign @kubernetes/api-reviewers 

My understanding is that this is a breaking change and is not backward compatible. So it will be hard to enforce this even if it is semantically correct. Perhaps some warning may be useful in this case.
